about: Horse Drawing is a pencil sketch of a horse that starts out as a beautifully shaded, realistic study at the tail and hindquarters, then slides into flat outline in the middle and ends as a childish scribble at the front: stick legs, a smiley face, a lopsided ear. It perfectly captures running out of time or energy halfway through a job. People use it to show a project that began with great care and ended in a rush, or anything whose quality fell off as it went on, like a TV series in its later seasons.
usage:
There are three labels across the top, one above each stage of the horse. The left box goes over the detailed rear, the middle over the half-shaded body, and the right over the scribbled head. Put the stages of something in order from best to worst: the first, second and last week of a project, or the intro, middle and conclusion of an essay.

The right-hand label is the punchline, so make it the most honest admission. Specific stages ("day 1 of the diet", "day 3", "day 5") read better than vague words.
